places.name: The Brow
ask: Its brow. Every god keeps a drawer of faces. Three of them, blind, out of the deck. It only gets to wear one.
The brow first. A face. It came up without one. Pull three, face down, and we'll see who's in the drawer.

places.name: The Heart
ask: The heart. What it's after. They're all after marrow, whatever they call it. Three, blind.
Over the heart, now. Something wants it back. Draw three, and don't look.

places.name: The Left Hand
ask: Left hand. Something was in its hand when it came up out of the Red. Three from the deck. Blind.
The left hand. It's holding on to something. They always are. Draw three, and we'll see what.

places.name: The Right Hand
ask: Right hand. What it lets go of. Something always stays on the step with the rest. Three, face down.
The right hand opens. Old Scythe keeps a count. Pull three, and leave him something to count.

places.name: The Belly
ask: The belly. That's where the fear sits. It'll lie about this one. The cards won't. Three, blind.
Down in the belly. Three, little hide, face down, where the fear can be counted.

places.name: The Feet
ask: The feet. A road. It came up a stair out of a pool an hour ago. Give it a road anyway. A road's a kindness. Draw three.
Feet. Three roads, face down. It'll have walked one of them by mourning.

places.name: Under It, in the Red
ask: And one under it. Face down, in the Red. We haven't read that one yet. Read. Red. Always red.
The last goes underneath, where the Red is. Leave it lying. It'll turn when it's ready.

weave.belly: Down in the belly, it's afraid of {p}.
weave.under: And under it, in the Red, face down till now, {p}. {w} wears that one.

open: There. Look at it lying there.
Well. That's the hide of it. ...And what's hid in it.

shapes.many_rev: Most of it lies the wrong way up. Good. So does everything here.
shapes.none_rev: Not one card turned against it. That's never happened. ...That's never good.
shapes.heart_belly: It's afraid of the very thing it wants. They always are.
shapes.hands: Both hands full of the same thing. It'll drop one.
shapes.calling: More {a} in it than it knows. It'll find out.
shapes.under_rev: And the one underneath is lying too.

close: Isn't it horrible? A moment ago it was nothing, and it was so quiet.
Up you get, then. The mouth's that way.
Go on. The sand's waiting. It always is.

brow: On the brow, the face it shows the Hide. {G}. That's what they'll see coming. Whether it's true is another card.
So that's the face it wears. {G}. Faces are lent here. It'll give this one back, one day.
heart: Over the heart lies what it wants, and what it wants is {g}. It'll walk the whole Hide for that, and never know why.
That's what's in its heart, then. {G}. Wanting is the oldest thing on the Hide. Older than the Hide.
lhand: The left hand holds what it won't put down, and that's {g}. It came up out of the pool already holding it.
The left hand closes, and what's in it is {g}. It won't open, not for anything. Watch it try.
rhand: The right hand opens, and what it lets go is {g}. Something always stays on the step with the rest. Old Scythe counts it.
What it gives up is {g}. It won't miss it. Not yet.
belly: Down in the belly, where the fear lives. {G}. Mind that one. Fear's the only thing here that never lies.
So that's what it's afraid of. {G}. Good. The ones afraid of nothing go first.
feet: Under the feet, the road that brought it. {G}. Roads don't end on the Hide. They just stop.
It came here by {g}. It'll leave by it too. That's how roads are.
under: And under it all, in the Red, face down till now. {G}. That's the one that's been doing the drawing. All along.

deck_open: Twenty-two of them, cut from hide and older than the count. Every one has lain on a body before this one. They remember the shape. Pick, and they'll tell it what it is. They already know.
The deck. Feel it? Warm, like something that's been held a long while. It's read every one that came up out of that pool. It knows this one. It's only being polite.
drawn: It didn't take that card. That card took it. They always do.
The deck reads the hand before the hand reads the deck. It's been waiting for this hand.
Hear that? A card comes off the deck the way a tooth comes out. Something's left a gap.
Don't look so pleased. Nobody chooses. The cards come up the way the dead come up, when they're ready.
There. It reached, and the deck let it. The deck doesn't let everyone.
Warm where it touched. They like this one. That's never good.
drawn_rev: Upside down. It came to it that way on purpose. The deck has a sense of humour, and no mercy.
Reversed. The card's lying. Or it's telling the truth the wrong way up. Same thing, here.
Head down, like the drowned. The deck turned this one over itself. Let's see why.
close_sum: Here's what the cards made of it, all together. Don't ask which card did which. They won't say.

open: Listen. This is how it goes, for this one.
Sit, then. I'll tell it the way the cards told me.
Here's the story of it. It's a short one. They all are, here.
feet: It came the way of {p}, though it won't remember the road.
Its feet knew the way of {p} before it ever stood up out of the pool.
brow: It rose out of the Red wearing the face of {p}, and the face was still wet.
When it came up, the face it had on was the face of {p}. It'll wear it a long while.
heart: What it wanted, more than anything, was {g}. It wouldn't have said so. It didn't have to.
Down where the wanting lives, it wanted {g}, and it would walk the whole Hide for it.
belly: What it feared was {g}. That fear will keep it alive longer than any blade.
And under the wanting, the fear. {G}. It'll meet that one again. Fears come round.
lhand: In its left hand it carried a thing it would not put down, and the thing was {g}.
What it held on to, with the left hand, was {g}, and nothing on the Hide would make it let go.
rhand: With the right it let something go, and what it let go was {g}. It won't miss it until much later.
And the right hand opened, and what fell out of it was {g}. The step kept that, with all the rest.
under: But that was only the top of it. Under all of it, face down in the Red the whole time, lay the card that did the drawing, {p}. {W} wears that one now. One day it might be this one's turn.
That's what lay on top. Underneath, in the Red, where nobody looks, it was {p} all along. {W} has that one now. Mantles change hands. That's what hands are for.
close: That's the story. It isn't finished. They never are.
And that's where it begins. Go on. The sand's waiting. It always is.
Isn't it horrible? A moment ago it was nothing, and it was so quiet.
tale.prophecy: And the last thing the cards said, they said to it, not to me.
go: Now up, and look into the mirror. The black one, in the face's mouth. Nothing looks back from it. Walk on into it anyway. There's no door here, and there never was. Only that.
There's the way out, in the great face's mouth. The black mirror. Go and look into it. It won't show this one. It doesn't show anyone. Step into the dark of it, and the sand's on the other side.
Go on, then. The mirror, there, in the mouth of the face. Look into it till it looks like nothing, and walk in. ...And don't look back. There's nothing to see, and it'll mind.

on.brow: On the brow it would mean {g}.
on.heart: Over the heart it would mean {g}.
on.lhand: In the left hand it would mean {g}.
on.rhand: What the right hand lets go would be {g}.
on.belly: In the belly it would mean {g}.
on.feet: Under the feet it would mean {g}.

brow: Three faces, turned up. It can wear one. The others go back in the drawer.
There. Three came up for the brow. Choose. Choosing is the only freedom the deck allows, and it lies about that.
heart: Three for the heart, face up now. What does it want? Go on. It's allowed to want.
The heart. Three of them, face up, and every one of them hungry.
lhand: Three it drew for the left hand. What does it hold on to? Pick, and it'll never put it down.
Left hand. Three things it might be holding, turned up. Only one fits the hand.
rhand: Three it drew for the right hand. What does it let go of? Choose what to lose. That's a kindness. Most never get to.
Right hand. Something has to fall out of it. Three came up. Pick the one it can spare.
belly: Three for the belly. Choose its fear. ...Choose carefully. It'll meet that one again.
The belly. Three fears, face up. It only gets to keep one.
feet: Three roads, turned up. It came by one of them. Pick which, and it'll remember the walking.
The feet. Three roads lie open, and every one of them ends here.

chose: Chosen. The other two go back in the deck. Now let's see if the deck agrees.
That one. The deck had a feeling it would. The rest go home.
Good. The other two go back in, and they'll remember being passed over.
turned: ...And the deck turns it over as it lands. It chose. The deck chose back.
Head down. It chose that card; the card chose to lie the other way. That's how choosing goes here.

mantles.one: the one who ends the turn
mantles.rev: the one who begins the next
mantles.say: The Unwritten. A page nobody's put a word on. The last one who held it out the whole age long never wrote anything, and the age ended anyway. Blank isn't empty. Blank is waiting.
mantles.say_rev: Turned over, and it's still blank. Worse. That means it's been written and wiped, again and again, until the page wore thin. You can see through it if you hold it to the fire. Don't.
mantles.gist: a turn nobody has taken yet
mantles.gist_rev: a story already told too many times

mantles.one: the one who walks and does not know why
mantles.say: The Pilgrim. Walking. Always walking, a staff and a hood and no idea where. The pilgrim road's worn a trench in the Hide a man deep, and everyone in it is walking to something that's already dead.
mantles.say_rev: The Pilgrim, sat down at the side of the road with its boots off. Some stop because they've arrived. Most stop because the road ran out under them. The road always runs out.
mantles.gist: to keep walking and never ask where
mantles.gist_rev: to stop, at last, and not get up

mantles.one: the one who buries
mantles.rev: the one who digs them up
mantles.say: The Gravedigger's Hands. Dirt under every nail and no memory of whose graves. The hands remember for it. They dig straight and they dig deep and they never once look in.
mantles.say_rev: The Hands, digging up. What was put down for a reason is coming back for one. The Ossuary Matron lays the dead in their order; these hands undo it.
mantles.gist: to bury what it cannot carry
mantles.gist_rev: to dig up what was put down for a reason

mantles.one: the one drawn to the light that burns it
mantles.wears: the moths with the white faces
mantles.say: The Singed Veil. A moth with a white face, going round and round the one light that'll burn it. The moths in the high court wear faces like that. They know what the light does. They go anyway.
mantles.say_rev: The Veil, already burned. Nothing left to draw it now, and nothing left to lose. It's lighter, burned. Ask anything that's been in a fire.
mantles.gist: the light that burns it
mantles.gist_rev: nothing, now; it has already burned

mantles.one: the one who is carried
mantles.rev: the knife that cut the cloth
mantles.wears: every child the Deep asks for
mantles.say: The Swaddling. Wrapped tight against the ash and carried. On the Hide somebody's always carried and somebody always carries, and the one who carries never puts it down, not even to sleep.
mantles.say_rev: The Swaddling, cut open. Somebody took a knife to the cloth. Maybe to free what was in it. Maybe not. The Deep asks for children, and somebody always pays.
mantles.gist: to be carried, and to carry
mantles.gist_rev: the knife that cuts the cloth

mantles.one: the one who ends
mantles.rev: the one who keeps it under
mantles.say: The Gleaner. Old Scythe himself, down in his pit under the bone. He comes up once an age to take the harvest, and he has never missed one. Not one stalk. Not one.
mantles.say_rev: The Gleaner, reversed, is the one who keeps him under. An Ossuarch with a sliver of the scythe in his plate, counting, always counting, so the old harvester stays down a little longer.
mantles.gist: the end that comes for everything
mantles.gist_rev: to keep the end under, a little longer

mantles.one: the one who suffers to be believed
mantles.rev: the crowd that came to watch
mantles.say: The Weeping Saint. She bleeds so they'll believe her, and they do; they always do. The girl in the iron wept until the weeping was the only thing left of her, and they made a faith of the tears.
mantles.say_rev: The Saint, reversed, is the crowd that came to watch her. A thousand faces and not one of them looking at her. They came for the weeping. They'd come again.
mantles.gist: to suffer, so as to be believed
mantles.gist_rev: to watch, and do nothing

mantles.one: the one who reads until it is read
mantles.say: The Scholar's Eye. Reads, and reads, and reads, until the page starts reading back. The oldest reader in the Citadel still sits at his book. He hasn't turned a page in an age. The page turns him.
mantles.say_rev: The Eye, turned inward. The eyes in the Needle, looking back. Once they've seen you, they don't stop. ...It looked. It shouldn't have looked.
mantles.gist: to know, whatever knowing costs
mantles.gist_rev: the eyes that look back

mantles.one: the one a breath behind
mantles.say: The Hanged Twin. Hung head down over still water, and in the water its twin stands upright, a breath behind it. Every still surface has one. The Drowned Twin keeps very good time.
mantles.say_rev: The Twin, a breath ahead. Worse. That one knows where it's going, and it's only waiting for this one to catch up. It will. They always do.
mantles.gist: a twin a breath behind it
mantles.gist_rev: a twin a breath ahead, waiting

mantles.one: the one that eats to keep
mantles.say: The Knot of Mouths. Many mouths and one hunger, eating to keep and keeping to eat. The Second Mouth preaches it. The Tallow-Mother lives it. Round and round it goes.
mantles.say_rev: The Knot, reversed. The one that's eaten. Someone has to be the meal. Somebody always is. Better to know which one you are.
mantles.gist: to eat, and keep what it eats
mantles.gist_rev: to be eaten

mantles.one: the one that burns down to give light
mantles.rev: the dark at the edge of the light
mantles.say: The Wick. It burns down to give a little light, and the light is all that's left of it. Every lantern on the Hide has one inside, a soul that chose to stay and burn instead of going out with the breath.
mantles.say_rev: The Wick, reversed, is the dark just past the edge of the light. Always there. Always patient. The light only ever pushes it back a step.
mantles.gist: to burn itself down for a little light
mantles.gist_rev: the dark at the edge of every light

mantles.one: the one who cuts her hair
mantles.say: The Mourner. She cuts her hair for every one the Red takes, and the Red takes them all. The Grandmother of the Red has none left. She cuts it anyway. The shore folk say you can hear the scissors in the surf.
mantles.say_rev: The Mourner, reversed, is the one being mourned. ...Somebody, somewhere, cut their hair for it already. Long before it came up out of the pool.
mantles.gist: grief that cuts and keeps cutting
mantles.gist_rev: to be mourned, and not know it

mantles.one: the one who locks the count
mantles.say: The Ossuary Key. It locks the count. Nine, and nine, and nine, and every bone in its place. The Pale Order's whole faith is a key turned in a lock, and the lock is the world.
mantles.say_rev: The Key, reversed. The one who opens it. Somebody always does. That's why there's a key. That's why there's always somebody looking for it.
mantles.gist: to lock the count and keep it
mantles.gist_rev: to open what was locked

mantles.one: the one who asks at the door
mantles.say: The Beggar's Cup. It knocks at the door with an empty bowl and asks, very politely, for marrow. The Ghauul ask like that. So does hunger. So does the Hide.
mantles.say_rev: The Cup, reversed, is the house that answers the door. Don't answer the door. Whatever knocks at night on the Hide, don't answer.
mantles.gist: to ask, and keep on asking
mantles.gist_rev: to open the door to what knocks

mantles.one: the one who rings under the water
mantles.say: The Drowned Bell. It rings under the water where nobody living hears it. The drowned king's court still walks down the old one's spine to the sound of it, in step, the whole way.
mantles.say_rev: The Bell, reversed, and rung in tune at last. That should frighten anybody. A drowned bell isn't meant to sound right.
mantles.gist: a call only the drowned can hear
mantles.gist_rev: a bell rung true, for once

mantles.one: the one who sells at the end of the world
mantles.say: The First Coin. Somebody sold something at the end of the world, and here's what they got for it. The merchant on the shore picks the dead clean and sells it back. Somebody's always selling.
mantles.say_rev: The Coin, reversed. The one who buys. What did it buy? ...No. Don't tell me. I'd rather not know what it paid.
mantles.gist: to sell what is left
mantles.gist_rev: to buy, and pay too much

mantles.one: the one that hardens what is given to it
mantles.say: The Kiln. It hardens what's given to it. Soft goes in, and doesn't come out soft. The Deep sets the old one's blood to iron in the dark under everything, slowly, the way a kiln does.
mantles.say_rev: The Kiln, reversed, is the one that cracks in the firing. Something always cracks. Better it cracks in the fire than after.
mantles.gist: to be hardened by what it goes through
mantles.gist_rev: to crack in the fire

mantles.one: the one who unpicks
mantles.say: The Unravelling Loom. Somebody's picking it apart, thread by thread, and humming while they do it. The Crone behind her veil pulls out what was woven wrong. It's mostly woven wrong.
mantles.say_rev: The Loom, reversed. The one who weaves it back. Badly. Knots and lumps, threads from somebody else's life. But it holds. Mostly it holds.
mantles.gist: to be unpicked, thread by thread
mantles.gist_rev: to be stitched back together, badly

mantles.one: the one who keeps what is lost
mantles.rev: the one who lets it go
mantles.say: The Lantern-Wright. The one who made the lanterns, and kept what was lost inside them. The makers were hunted out. There are fewer lanterns every year, and nobody left who knows how.
mantles.say_rev: The Wright, reversed, is the one who lets it go. The light goes out the top, they say, like breath. Some of them want to go. Most of them do.
mantles.gist: to keep what was lost
mantles.gist_rev: to let go what it kept

mantles.one: the one who holds the note
mantles.say: The Drowned Choir. Under the crypts they're still holding the note. They've held it so long the stone hums with it, and the water in the low places shivers when you walk by.
mantles.say_rev: The Choir, reversed, is the rest between the notes. Listen. ...There. That. That's what they're afraid of.
mantles.gist: to hold on past all breath
mantles.gist_rev: the silence between notes

mantles.one: the one who owes
mantles.rev: the one who comes to collect
mantles.say: The Tithe. It owes. Everyone left owes a tenth of everything, back to whatever gave them the mourning. Nobody remembers taking the loan. Everybody pays.
mantles.say_rev: The Tithe, reversed. The one who comes to collect. On foot, at night, very polite. Knock, knock. Not the tenth, this time. The rest.
mantles.gist: to owe, and pay
mantles.gist_rev: the one who comes to collect

mantles.one: the one whose orders are never obeyed
mantles.rev: the city that would obey if it could
mantles.wears: the Man in the Rust, on the dark moon
mantles.say: The Hollow Crown. Orders, given and given, and nobody obeying. The Man in the Rust sits up on the dark moon and still gives them. The Hide doesn't listen. It never did.
mantles.say_rev: The Crown, reversed, is the city that would obey if it could. It can't. It's empty. Not one left in it to hear the orders.
mantles.gist: to command, and not be obeyed
mantles.gist_rev: to want to obey, and have nothing left
